messages.subject: Interpreting Results
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am new to SCR analysis and am working on creating a spatially explicit multi-session model for a dataset that was previously analyzed in a non-spatial framework. I need a little help interpreting the results and estimating population size. What is the scale of the density estimate? Is it the area of the trap grid or the area of the state space? This is might be complicated because the trap arrays were irregularly shaped (See below).
 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-_Gmjkz1e_y0/WiV4Ui0iIVI/AAAAAAAAAes/zAwX9tIKC54pDA0i4TfpeF7necznuh7IQCLcBGAs/s1600/TrapGrid_S.JPG>

Any guidance would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Jennie

messages.body_plain:
hi Jennie,
  The intercept of the density model is log(expected number of activity centers per state-space pixel). e.g., if the result comes out to be -1 then exp(-1) = 0.368 individuals per pixel.  If the state-space is 500m x 500m then this is a density of 0.368*4 per km^2.  If you have 1000 state-space pixels then the estimated population size for the entire state-space is 368 individuals.
 Hope this helps!
regards
andy

messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

Amazing, thank you so much for your prompt suggestions. I adapted my script to match your changes - the biggest change was defining the state space data frame using the make.ssDF function (as opposed to importing pixel coordinates) and trimming the state space as an argument to the model fitting function. Even when keeping the 250m resolution the models run much faster, but I also reduced the resolution to 1km as Andy suggested which greatly improved run time as well. As a result I can run models the full dataset with spatial covariates in under 3 hours, which is orders of magnitude faster. So, it worked! Also good to know about the binomial models.

Just wondering, I noticed that there is a huge jump in the AIC values (ie. >200) when the models incorporate any of the spatial covariates in the rsfDF. Is this really suggesting that the spatial covariates are not contributing to space use by this species, as compared to the null model and models with just behavioral variables like sex? Or does the addition of the RSF make it so that the models are not really comparable by AIC to models without spatial covariates? Hope that question is clear, but let me know if I can clarify.

Again thanks for your help, much appreciated!

Nina

Hello,

Key point is that you must be able to define a covariate for _every_ point in the ssDF.

If you have say a raster of come covariate you wish to use to describe density, say ‘cov.rast’, then for a single session state space, you could use the extract function in the raster package:

ssDF[[1]]$covariate <- extract(cov.rast,

                               SpatialPoints(cbind(ssDF[[1]]$X, ssDF[[1]]$Y)))

oSCR has a helper function to do this too called ‘extract.rast()’. You supply a raster and an ssDF object and a few other arguments related to how you want the summary to be done. This is not documented up as I still need to do some better testing on it.

Chris
